Convention Preview
Psi Upsilon Fraternity lias announced its 159th
Convention
schedule, a memorable series of events and activities for four
days in June. Marco Island, Florida will lx* the site of the
Convention scheduled forJune 22-25, 2002 at the Marco
Island Marriott Resort and Golf Club.
Brothers from around the United States and Canada will
gather to recognize Psi Upsilon'
s many accomplishments,
educate members on new programming initiatives, and
celebrate brotherhood. All members of the fraternity are
invited to participate.
Psi Upsilon brothers will convene at the opening session
Saturday evening,June 22. Plans for the weekend include a
golf tournament on Sunday morning.
The 159
,h
Convention is going to be an exciting time. Not
only will we celebrate brotherhood and the freedoms we
enjoy in our great nations, our programming is bound to
motivate members to return to their chapters with an invigorating outlook for the future. We hope to inspire brothers of all
ages to embrace the core values of Psi Upsilon and put them
to work in their daily lives.

Gaining the Professional Advantage
Would you feel comfortable interviewing for a job over
dinner? Do you understand foreign customs that might affect
your ability to work with clients from other countries? You
never get a second chance to make a first
impression. As a certified businessetiquette
consultant, Nonnie Cameron Owens travels
across the country facilitating etiquette,
image and interpersonal skills programs for
corporations and colleges. She created her
company, Etiquette Plus, after retiring from
a 32-year airline career, which took her
around the world. Recently she completed a
training packet titled, " Nonnie Cameron'
s
Etiquette Library." She will share the skills
and insights of this comprehensive etiquette library with us,
giving us her secrets for how to obtain the competitive edge
in today's job market.
2002 Leadership Institute
The 2002 Leadership Institute curriculum will include programs focused on success in college and beyond and etiquette
standards in the work place and social settings. There will also
be team building activities on the beach and roundtable
discussions of chapter best practices.

Challenges & Choices
In this session you will be introduced to Challenges&Choices,
a program already undertaken by some chapters and available
to all, which is designed to assist members in making better
choices when faced with challenges. This will be a preview of
the Challenges&Choices weekend, here dealing with ritual,
respect for property, and confrontation - three of the nine
Basic Expectations of a fraternity member. You will also learn
how to bring a Challenges&Choices retreat to your chapter.

Dennis Tito, Delta '
62 (New York University), became the world's first non-astronaut
to leave the atmosphere, when he traveled to the International Space Station on April 30,
2001. Though Star City, where the Soyuz shuttle landed sounds like it might be a knock
off of Hollywood, it is in actuality, Russia's equivalent of Cape Canaveral.
Tito, who was fifty-nine years old when he made the trip, wras adamant about his
plans, " I've been on this planet for 60 years and now?
I have a chance to get off' he
said.

Brandon K.Schaefer,

The Russian Space Agency called the three-man crew of the Soyuz " its first international crew." The two astronauts w ho accompanied him are Russian and Kazakh.
Russia firing an American into space could be instrumental in defrosting hard feelings
left over from the Cold War, but since the accomplishment, Tito's name has been kicked
around in the American press. At the same time his venture was warmly received by the
Russian press and people. Why isn't Tito's voyage equally recognized as an achievement?
NASA, who Tito used to work for as an engineer, was vehemently opposed to sending
him up. Tito said of himself that he has been the target of " professional jealousy" from
astronauts and he has been poked fun at on Comedy Central and late night television.
Tito paid this price, along with the $20 million that he gave to the Russian Space
Agency, for the experience. He also was required to sign a waiver to the effect of " you
break it, you buy it." Tito, who made his money by founding Wilshire Associates, a highpowered money management firm, felt that he was well covered. His company currently
handles $11 billion in investment and pension funds and is well known for the Wilshire
5000 stock index, a favorite indicator of Alan Greenspan s.
Brother Tito's badge didn't appear on the list of items he told CNN he would be
carrying, such as a camera, CD player, and some personal photographs, but then again,
we are a fraternity accustomed to secrecy, so maybe he just didn't admit it to the press
that the clasped hands would be pinned on his breast beneath his space suit.
" This is not a vacation." Tito quipped, " It's the fulfillment of a life's dream to fly into
space."
